unclassified audited source rows fail certification

phases.instructions: Build the generic scoreboard first. Prefer compiler-led discovery and typed inventory/deletion rows over prose. Do not begin crate cleanup beyond what is needed to expose and classify the roots.
phases.qa_focus: Inventory completeness, deletion-ledger action honesty, no filename-only classification, no production debt hidden as certification language.

plan: Adversarial constraint: at production scale, Phase 1 breaks if any audited Worth source under worth-topo, worth-spatial, worth-kernel, or the consumed worth-query graph-obligation facade can still compile by passing a lower-authority artifact (support report, crate adoption status, admitted handoff, raw evidence rows, string stage link, copied split/loop digest, synthetic fixture, or residue literal) into a production graph-authority boundary while the inventory classifies only by search/prose. Quantitative target: 0 unclassified audited Rust source files in scoped production roots, 0 deletion-target rows allowed as keep without a distinct authority proof, and one discovery record plus one lower-authority promotion guard plan for each root authority family before crate cleanup begins.

Create the generic cross-crate scoreboard before any cleanup. Add a narrow module, preferably under crates/worth-kernel/src/query_graph_authority_gate/ because worth-kernel already owns cross-crate Worth query-adoption reports, with typed rows for WorthGraphAuthorityInventoryRow, WorthGraphAuthorityDeletionLedgerRow, WorthGraphAuthorityDiscoveryRecord, and WorthLowerAuthorityPromotionGuardPlan. The row vocabulary must encode owner crate/subsystem, authority class, deletion target class, discovery source (compiler, compile-fail, public-facade, certification-only, search-seed), action (keep, collapse, delete, residue, query-gap), replacement surface/blocker, and QA evidence reference. Do not model these as strings except for stable source paths and evidence labels.

Build validation before population. The report constructor must reject duplicate source ids, empty owner/subsystem/responsibility/replacement fields, deletion-target rows marked keep without a distinct-authority justification, residue rows without owner/cap/introduced-phase/removal-trigger, query-gap rows without a named Query blocker, and any audited source path that has no inventory row. This is the load-bearing harness; later crate cleanup depends on these denials.

Implement audited-source discovery as a test/certification helper, not as prose. Walk only the Phase 1 audited roots in the spec: crates/worth-topo/src/topology_operators/adoption, crates/worth-topo/src/construction/query_native_boundary, crates/worth-spatial/src/query_adoption, crates/worth-spatial/src/workload_platform/evidence_ledger and 7.3/7.4 boolean evidence paths, crates/worth-kernel/src/query_adoption, crates/worth-kernel/src/construction/query_authority, crates/worth-kernel/src/construction/graph_obligation_adoption, crates/worth-kernel/src/construction/phase_chain, crates/worth-kernel/src/construction/result_surface, crates/worth-kernel/src/workload_composition, and the worth-query facade/docs surfaces consumed for graph obligation authority. Certification must fail on a seeded unclassified .rs path so drift cannot silently become implicit residue.

Seed root authority family discovery records from actual surfaces before feature cleanup: topology operator graph obligation adoption/catalog/residue/proof, topology query-native handoff/admission/compose execution, spatial query adoption and evidence-stage index/stage links, kernel construction query authority/support summary, kernel graph obligation adoption selector/family execution matrices, kernel phase-chain admitted scaffold and result surface, workload evidence/split/loop handoffs, and worth-query Consumer Kit/Graph Touch Obligation facade exports. Each record must name the intentional compiler-led break to try later, the expected downstream failures it should expose, and the final enforced API target that will replace the break.

Build the deletion ledger in parallel with the inventory. Seed rows for duplicate support reports, local support-pin wrappers, blueprint proof-obligation rows, local ceremony audits, handoff-only result helpers, raw evidence-row scan helpers, copied evidence-row vectors, string-prefix/stage-link helpers, synthetic proof fixtures, compatibility reports, and residue manifests. Initial actions may be collapse/delete/residue/query-gap/certification-only only when backed by the typed row; do not classify production deletion targets as keep unless the row proves a distinct boundary not carried by Query, split ledger, loop ledger, or receipt proof.

Make the lower-authority promotion compile-fail plan explicit in code even before all trybuild cases exist. Add guard-plan rows for: support report is not graph authority; crate-level Query adoption is not graph obligation proof; admitted handoff is not executed birth; raw evidence rows are not an evidence-stage index; string-prefix stage links are not typed receipt linkage; split ledger digest is not loop ledger digest; synthetic graph authority fixture is not production proof; residue row literal is not a certified residue manifest. Point each planned guard at the future ui test path and required stronger type.

Add focused Phase 1 tests around the scoreboard constructor and coverage rules first: machine-readable inventory and deletion ledger instantiate; duplicate/unclassified/invalid residue rows fail; seeded unclassified audited source fails; root discovery records cover all root families; deletion-target keep without distinct authority proof fails; compile-fail guard plan contains all lower-authority promotion cases. Only after these pass should later phases demote/private/seal real crate APIs.

Keep crate cleanup out of Phase 1 except tiny exposure needed to classify root families. If an implementation step reveals a missing Query graph-obligation capability, record a query-gap row with blocker and stop the affected coverage from certifying; do not add a Worth-local substitute.

phases.instructions: Pin the Query surfaces Worth may consume before rewriting crate internals. Keep this phase short and contract-focused; do not build Worth-local substitutes for missing Query capabilities.
phases.qa_focus: Query proof vocabulary exactness, Consumer Kit usage, no local required-family lists, no fabricated receipts, query-gap rows for real blockers.

plan: Adversarial constraint: Phase 2 breaks at production scale if any Worth code path can satisfy a graph-authority API with a Worth-local adoption/status/support artifact instead of a Query-owned executed graph obligation proof. Quantitative target: 0 Worth-local types may type-check where a Query graph execution proof is required; every required contract family maps to exactly one canonical worth_query public facade surface; every missing Query capability is recorded as a typed query-gap row with owner, blocker, and no local substitute.

Pin the canonical Query contract vocabulary first. Create or extend a short WORTH Query contract-baseline test/document under crates/worth-query/tests or docs that names the public surfaces Worth may consume: graph_obligation_consumer_kit, WORTHQueryGraphObligationConsumerRegistrationDeclaration, WORTHQueryGraphObligationSelectorCoverageDeclaration, WORTHQueryGraphObligationSupportPin, WORTHQueryGraphObligationResidueManifest, WORTHQueryGraphObligationAdoptionProof, WORTHQueryGraphObligationExecutionProof, WORTHQueryGraphObligationInMemoryProof, WORTHQueryGraphTouchDescriptor, WORTHQueryGraphTouchSelector, WORTHQueryGraphObligationOperatingWorldDescriptor, WORTHQueryGraphObligationRegistration, WORTHQueryGraphObligationSupportMatrix, WORTHQueryGraphObligationSupportPosture, WORTHQueryGraphObligationSupportLane, WORTHQueryGraphObligationKind, WORTHQueryGraphObligationExecutionInput, WORTHQueryGraphObligationExecutionResultRow, and WORTHQueryGraphObligationExecutionResultEnvelope. The baseline must cite crates/worth-query/src/facade.rs exports and the Graph Touch Obligation/Consumer Kit docs, not Worth-local wrappers.

Model the Worth-facing contract as a small typed matrix before adding behavior. Required rows: adoption posture, selector coverage, support pinning, selected obligation proof, executed obligation proof, graph obligation receipt/result envelope, residue manifest, local-ceremony audit, and capability-gap posture. Each row must name the canonical Query facade type/function, the acceptance role it satisfies, and whether it is execution-required or selection-only. Selection-only adoption must be explicitly marked insufficient for Worth graph-authority closeout.

Add the anti-substitution proof next. Use the existing WORTH Query trybuild harness pattern in tests/phase_boundaries_graph_obligation_compile_fail.rs and tests/ui/graph_obligation/consumer_kit to add fixtures proving crate-level adoption status, support snapshots, local ceremony audits, local required-family lists, in-memory selection-only proof, and residue manifests cannot be passed to APIs that require WORTHQueryGraphObligationExecutionProof or an adoption proof produced by prove_adoption_with_execution(). If an existing public API is too broad to express this, tighten the API or record a query-gap row rather than creating a Worth adapter.

Add the positive contract smoke test only after the negative proof shape exists. Extend graph_obligation_consumer_kit_facade.rs or add a focused Phase 2 test that constructs the full public facade path: registration declaration, selector coverage, support pin against WORTHQueryGraphObligationSupportMatrix::milestone_9_9_authority_surface(), evaluated local ceremony audit, residue manifest, prove_execution_with(...), and prove_adoption_with_execution(). Assert the manifest carries an execution proof digest, the execution proof has real executor rows, selected obligation count is nonzero, and residue rows are explicit.

Represent missing Query capability blockers as query-gap rows, not Worth-local substitutes. If the baseline discovers that a required Worth adoption need has no Query facade surface, add a typed query-gap row in the Phase 1 scoreboard registry if the dependency is in Worth scope, or a WORTH Query contract-baseline gap row if the work is confined to worth-query. Each row must name the missing Query surface, owning crate/team, blocked Worth deletion/adoption class, and the test that proves no local fallback is accepted.

Keep Phase 2 contract-focused. Do not rewrite worth-topo, worth-spatial, or worth-kernel internals during this phase except for a minimal query-gap row if required by the contract. Do not add Worth-local Consumer Kit wrappers, local support pin lists, fabricated receipts, or local graph execution summaries. Later crate phases consume the pinned Query contract and perform cleanup.

Build the load-bearing closeout matrix before adding documentation. Extend worth-kernel's query_graph_authority_gate surface or a sibling certification module with typed closeout rows that join the Phase 1 inventory row, deletion ledger row, root authority family, final disposition, ordinary public facade accessor, compile-fail/public-boundary evidence, residue metadata, Query-gap metadata, and exact source coverage proof. The constructor must reject duplicate source ids, missing Phase 1 audited sources, deletion-target classes with no final row, undocumented residue/gap rows, public-facade fields that point only to private internals, and evidence labels that do not resolve to a real test or fixture path.

Reuse the Phase 1 scoreboard as the source of truth, not as a copied table. Have the closeout certifier consume current_worth_graph_authority_gate_report(), current_worth_graph_authority_audited_source_paths(), current_worth_graph_authority_deletion_ledger(), and current_worth_lower_authority_promotion_guard_plan(); fail if any closeout matrix row disagrees with Phase 1 source-set counts/digests, deletion actions, lower-authority promotion cases, graph-obligation counters, or primitive-construction coverage. Define the final disposition vocabulary in types rather than strings: DeletedSurface, CollapsedCanonicalQueryProof, CollapsedSplitLedgerReceipt, CollapsedLoopLedgerReceipt, CertificationOnlyBoundary, ExplicitResidue, QueryCapabilityGap, and PublicFacadeStatusOnly. Residue rows must carry owner, cap, introduced phase, removal trigger, and public-boundary/compile-fail containment; Query gaps must carry the named missing Query capability and must block, not substitute for, covered-lane certification.

Add public closeout access through ordinary APIs while preserving sealed construction. The public facade should expose a read-only closeout report with adoption/proof posture, deletion/residue/query-gap counters by class, zero-silent-bypass status, and the accepted facade accessors for topo, spatial, kernel, and Query proof surfaces. Wire lower-authority rejection into closeout, not only into separate UI tests. Each sabotage must fail because the closeout matrix demands the stronger Query proof, split ledger receipt, loop ledger receipt, executed birth receipt, or typed evidence-stage product, not because of an unrelated missing import.

Close the public facade posture row by row. For worth-topo, confirm operator catalog/query-native boundary/blueprint residues expose only classification or Query-surface posture. For worth-spatial, confirm query adoption, evidence-stage index, stage-link, split ledger, and loop ledger surfaces expose typed receipts and counters without raw row substitution. For worth-kernel, confirm workload composition and construction authority expose executed graph authority and ledger-receipt handoffs without copied rows or handoff-only promotion.
